description:
FILED s449s (Opus, agent S of round 7), as the deliberate residue of #563.
Both spellings are PRE-EXISTING; #563's repair does not change either.

perl's `<PATTERN>` is `glob("PATTERN")`, and glob's argument is a
WHITESPACE-SEPARATED LIST of patterns (perlfunc; PCL already models this
since #450 in `p-glob`).  Two spellings lose it, on the two different parse
paths a `<...>` run can take:

(a) SILENT WRONG, the `>` survives so PExpr's rebuild owns it:

      my @f = sort <./gd/*.t ./gd/a.t>;
      perl: three names (a.t, a.t, b.t)
      PCL : (p-glob "./gd/*.t./gd/a.t")   <- the SPACE is gone

    `Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block` concatenates the token CONTENTS of
    the run to rebuild the pattern, and whitespace tokens are not in the run
    it is handed, so a multi-pattern diamond silently becomes one impossible
    pattern.  The fix has to recover the source text (the tokens are still
    linked into the document, so `previous_token`/`next_token` can see the
    whitespace), or move the rebuild to the source-level repair that #563
    added.

(b) DROPS LOUDLY, the derailed path (§14c):

      my @f = sort < ./g-*.t >;
      perl: the two names
      PCL : statement dropped -- "Handle single node of unknown type"

    `Pl::Parser2::_repair_glob_pattern_cascade` requires the pattern to be ONE
    CONTIGUOUS WORD (`next if $pat =~ /[\s<]/`).  That guard is deliberate and
    is documented in the function: it is the belt to `_ends_term`'s braces, so
    that a shape where `_ends_term` is wrong about term position cannot be
    rewritten into a glob.  s449s closed the two `_ends_term` gaps it found
    (`PPI::Token::ArrayIndex`, a deref block's `}`), so the guard may be
    relaxable -- but ONLY with a fresh search for the breaking case, i.e. a
    `X < ... /re.../ ... >` one-liner where X ends a term and `_ends_term`
    says it does not.  Do not relax it without that search.

BAR: both spellings vs perl (multi-pattern, spaced-single, and the
zero-match forms); the four `_ends_term`-gap probes from #563
(`$#a<3&&$s=~/a>b/`, `${$x}<3&&$s=~/a>b/`, `time < 2 && "ab" =~ /a>b/`,
`$h{k}<3&&$s=~/a>b/`) unchanged; corpus-diff; a row beside the #563 rows in
`Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t`, which carries a NOT-here comment naming this
task.
subject: A diamond glob pattern containing WHITESPACE is a LIST of patterns: `<./a b>` loses the space silently, `< ./a-* >` drops
